profiles.meeting_scenario: A Belgian healthcare law team is holding a coordination meeting to align workstreams for a client response to a forthcoming reform of multidisciplinary team (MDT) reimbursement and documentation rules in oncology care. The client is a hospital federation that wants to cite a population-based study on MDT uptake across seven invasive tumour types in Belgium to argue that MDT participation has improved but that administrative burden still discourages discussion of some patient groups, especially older patients. The meeting context is late in the drafting cycle: one workstream covers the formal consultation submission to the federal health authorities, and the other covers the supporting appendix summarizing the oncology evidence and the legal framing around use of administrative data and reimbursement language. The agenda is to confirm which draft is being circulated, what is included in the appendix, what counts as ready for client review, and who handles the filing package and final handoff. The expected outcome is apparent alignment on next steps so the client receives a reviewable package before the consultation deadline.

members.name: Elise Van den Broeck
members.role: Partner, Healthcare Regulatory and Public Law
members.expertise: Belgian hospital regulation, reimbursement frameworks, ministerial consultations, stakeholder submissions
members.background: Elise leads the firm's healthcare regulatory practice and previously advised on NIHDI/RIZIV implementation measures affecting hospital financing and care coordination.
members.private_state: She wants the federation to receive a polished strategic submission quickly so its policy director can react before the weekend, and she is trying to avoid reopening the scope of the drafting package or creating delay through over-lawyering.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the latest draft,' it refers to the clean consultation response she circulated by email that is suitable for client reading, not the internal document-management redline.
A document is 'ready for client review' once the argument structure and asks are stable, even if footnotes, bilingual alignment, and some formal citations are still being cleaned up.
The 'appendix on the seven tumours' is a concise evidentiary annex with headline trends from the published study, not a broader methodological or subgroup analysis package.
Friday is the internal client-delivery date to the federation's policy director, who will handle any onward circulation and formal submission steps.

members.name: Thomas De Smet
members.role: Senior Associate, Life Sciences Data and Health Information Law
members.expertise: Health-data governance, administrative database use, hospital confidentiality issues, drafting support annexes and compliance notes
members.background: Thomas previously worked in-house at a university hospital and now supports cross-border life sciences and healthcare matters involving data access, evidence annexes, and regulatory submissions.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid sending a draft that the client will treat as final before the authorities or member hospitals see a citation-checked and procedurally complete version, and he is concerned about factual precision in how the oncology evidence is described.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'the latest draft,' it refers to the most recent redline in the matter workspace, because that is the authoritative version showing all current edits and legal caveats.

A draft is only 'ready for client review' once citations, decree references, bilingual consistency, and formatting are sufficiently complete that the client can forward it externally without legal clean-up.

The 'appendix on the seven tumours' should include the subgroup findings highlighted in the study's implications, especially older patients and uptake variation over time, plus a short note on the administrative-data basis for the claims.
Friday is effectively the filing deadline for the whole package, so anything sent to the client should already be close to submission quality.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the latest draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the latest draft' of the submission package.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the clean email attachment titled 'Federation_MDT_Response_v7_clean.docx,' which she expects the client to read and mark up.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the document-management-system file 'MDR consultation v7.2 redline,' which contains newer edits on decree wording and caveats about the oncology evidence.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In legal teams, people often shorthand multiple near-identical versions as 'the latest draft,' and both assume the other is oriented to the same central working document because the file names and content are largely overlapping.

misalignment_points.topic: Meaning of ready for client review
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the package should be 'ready for client review' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this means the strategic narrative, requested policy changes, and main appendix structure are stable enough for the federation's policy director to react, even if some citations and language alignment are still being finalized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this means the package is substantively and formally complete enough that the client could forward it to member hospitals or treat it as near-final without further legal refinement.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds operationally standard and cooperative, and each lawyer's criterion is normal within their own sub-role, so neither feels a need to spell out what level of completeness 'client review' implies.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss 'the appendix on the seven tumours' as if it is a single obvious supporting document.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a short appendix with one table and brief narrative showing increased MDT discussion rates over time across the seven invasive tumour categories, mainly to support the policy point that MDTs have become standard but administrative burden remains a barrier.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the appendix to also cover subgroup patterns such as older patients being less often discussed, differences across years, and a short methodology note about population-based administrative databases so the claims are defensible if quoted outside the immediate consultation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both are talking about the same published study and using the same label for the annex, the boundary difference feels like detail within a shared task rather than a separate scope decision that would normally require explicit negotiation.
